newsitem.title: USA: Icahn says may remount RJR proxy fight.
newsitem.headline: Icahn says may remount RJR proxy fight.

text.p: Carl Icahn, who sold his 7.3 percent stake in RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp last night after his failed campaign to split RJR into separate food and tobacco companies, said he may in the future restart his proxy fight to accomplish the split.

In a prepared statement quoting from Icahn's U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission filing today on the stock sale, Icahn said "In the event that the market price for (RJR's) shares declines, they (affilates controlled by Icahn) may again determine that they could wage a successful proxy fight and thereby immediately effect the spinoff."

However, he stated "It would be exceedingly difficult at this time to prevail in a proxy contest" with RJR management due to recent "euphoria associated with speculation in the media concerning the increased possibility of a global settlement of tobacco litigation and a concurrent dramatic rise in tobacco stock prices...," according to the filing.
But tobacco analysts said they don't expect Icahn to again spar with RJR management, saying he is content to walk away with his huge windfall of about $114 million.

"He isn't coming back. What you should look at is that he made millions on a $300 million investment in 12 months. He is a smart guy who had the guts to buy the stock. It is another chapter in his book on how to make money on undervalued companies," said Gary Black, tobacco analyst at Sanford C. Bernstein.

Icahn also said in the statement that he does not see the current tobaccco litigation climate improving "and, therefore, the current (RJR) board of directors may never spin off (81 percent owned) Nabisco (Holdings Corp )."
He added that his average cost basis for the 19.9 million shares he sold for $36.75 each through Goldman Sachs was $30 per share.
On that basis, the position was amassed at a cost of about $617 million, holdings that likely cost Icahn only a $300 million outlay because of margin buying, analysts said.
Icahn or a spokesman was not immediately available to comment.
